correctness.rationale: For each integer n>=5 and h>0, established the exact relation between silhouette edges and sign changes of incident facet normals; the side-normal negatives form one contiguous block. The all-vertex event is equivalent to exactly one negative side normal. A centered Gaussian pair/triple sign identity yields singleton probability n(2 asin(t sin(pi/n))-asin(t sin(2pi/n)))/pi. Neighbors-negative implies middle-negative because cos(2pi/n)>0. All variables and n/h ranges are explicit, and limiting measure-zero orientations are excluded correctly. Squaring positive derivative terms shows a unique maximum at t=1/(sqrt(3)cos(pi/n)); uniform Taylor expansion gives the fixed-h and optimal n^-2 limits. Standalone code reconstructed actual planar convex hulls for n=5,6,8,12, three heights each, and checked high-precision asymptotic ratios; tests passed. Computation is corroboration only, not proof.

originality.rationale: The closest complete mathematical research record derives the n=4 right-rectangular-pyramid full-vertex law and excludes nonrectangular bases. Black--Criado supplies general bounds on expected shadow size, not a full-silhouette probability for regular n-gonal pyramids. For n >= 5, the number of silhouette vertices takes three or more values, so mean shadow size alone does not imply the maximal-vertex probability. In the surveyed full texts and semantic/exact-term searches no statement was found that implies the closed n>=5 formula, unique optimizing altitude, or sharp n^-2 maximum. This is positive best-knowledge originality assessment, not certification of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The event that all vertices of a pyramid survive a planar projection is the extremal-complexity event, a natural invariant in random-shadow complexity. Unlike the four-sided-base case, at n>=5 the count has several values; the event is not determined by the expected count. The theorem gives an exact probability for every n>=5 and aspect ratio, a unique height optimizer (a genuine all-shapes-within-this-natural-family classification), and the sharp n^-2 rarity with optimal constant and limiting optimal shape. This connects deterministic geometry, spherical normal cones, and dimension-dependent stochastic combinatorics and is not a bare parameter renaming or a known-table lookup.
